relations.subject: ui:import-documents-panel
relations.evidence: The **cbimport json** and **cbimport csv** command-line utilities should be used in preference to Couchbase Web Console whenever high-performance importing is required; and especially when the data-set to be imported is greater in size than 100 MB.

relations.subject: ui:import-documents-panel
relations.evidence: Before attempting to import data with Couchbase Web Console, ensure that the **Query Service** has been deployed on the cluster: data-import with Couchbase Web Console depends on this service.

relations.subject: ui:import-documents-panel
relations.evidence: Couchbase Server will parse the data within the file, thereby creating one or more JSON documents; which will be stored in the [Destination Bucket](#destination-bucket).

relations.subject: ui:import-documents-panel
relations.evidence: In the previous example, the bucket **testBucket** was selected, but no change was made to the default scope and collection settings; which were both **\_default**.

notable_absence.finding: This page never states which RBAC role is required to use the Import Documents panel, unlike the Backup UI (Full Admin) and the statistics Dashboard (Full Admin/Bucket Admin/etc.) elsewhere in this batch. Since importing writes data into a bucket, the omission is a real gap - a reader has no way to know from this page alone whether Bucket Admin-level access suffices.

cross_component_finding: The 'Value of Field' document-ID option describes upsert-like behavior in prose without ever naming it as such: 'when the selected field contains a value that is not unique across the bucket, the document will be imported into the bucket as an _update_ to a document that is already resident within the bucket, and shares the id specified by the value' - functionally the same replace-if-exists semantics as the promoted n1ql:upsert (UPSERT), but the page draws no connection between the two and uses the word 'update' rather than 'upsert'.
